summary: Singles' Day puts AI credits in the shopping cart, two factory surveys disagree, and carmakers sell more cars while earning far less.
body: Singles' Day, China's biggest shopping festival, is under way, and this year AI is on the shelf. Shoppers can buy "tokens", prepaid credits for using AI tools, from companies such as Alibaba, DeepSeek and ByteDance. On Monday, livestream seller Austin Li, known as the "Lipstick King", sold 100,000 monthly memberships to an Alibaba office AI in half an hour, Reuters reports [^1]. An analyst warned that paying in advance is risky because AI products change quickly [^1].

Two surveys of factories tell different stories. The private RatingDog/S&P Global index was 52.0 in October, which signals growth, while the official index was 49.3, which signals shrinking [^2][^3]. The private survey covers fewer firms and leans toward exporters [^2]. Caixin links the weakness to fewer overseas Christmas orders and slower spending at home after the October holiday [^3].

Cars show a similar split. Xiaomi delivered more than 50,000 electric cars in October, its best month this year, and Leapmotor passed 100,000 [^6][^7]. Yet carmakers' total profits fell 68% from a year earlier in September, which Caixin blames on "relentless price competition" [^5]. Cheap cars help buyers, but a long price war squeezes companies and their workers.

In tech, food-delivery giant Meituan released a large AI model it says was trained entirely on Chinese-made chips [^4]. In Taiwan, the ruling party proposed prison terms of up to 10 years for sending advanced AI chips to mainland China without approval, though the opposition-controlled legislature may block it [^8]. The World Internet Conference opened in Wuzhen with a focus on open-source AI; Chinese state media says more than 460 companies are exhibiting [^9][^10].
differences: October factory data conflict: the private RatingDog/S&P Global survey shows growth at 52.0, while the official survey shows contraction at 49.3, because they sample different firms [^2][^3]. The reports read for this brief do not name the chips Meituan used, so its claim cannot yet be checked independently [^4].
